answer: Graduated trust resists sybils by giving new identities almost no weight, like a young vine that must climb slowly before it bears fruit. An agent earns larger limits and voting power only after a history of attested good work, verified by independent peers. Each fake therefore costs an attacker weeks of consistent, useful behavior, and one detected fraud prunes the whole plume of accumulated trust back to zero. An ivory-tower score means nothing; only a proven record of real work moves an identity up, so flooding the network with fresh fakes buys no influence.
